en: The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the remaining old-growth forests of the Philippine islands.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the Constitution and settle actual controversies involving rights.
National hero Jose Rizal annotated Antonio de Morga's book Sucesos de las Islas Filipinas to prove that Filipinos had a rich culture before Spanish colonization.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape, which was formed by repeated layers of lava and ash from past eruptions.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains over 2,000 years ago using an ancient stone-walling technique and complex irrigation systems.
The waling-waling, scientifically known as Vanda sanderiana, is an epiphytic orchid native to the montane forests of Mindanao and is considered the queen of Philippine orchids.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen at least eighteen years of age has the right and duty to vote in national and local elections.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, from the balcony of his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift incubator made from bamboo and hot water bottles to provide medical care for newborns in rural areas.
During the Pahiyas Festival in Lucban, Quezon, farmers decorate their houses with colorful kipings, which are thin, leaf-shaped wafers made from ground rice.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where each consonant-vowel syllable is represented by a specific character, and it was traditionally written on bamboo or leaves.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over 600 species of fish and 360 species of corals, making it a vital marine biodiversity hotspot.
